question: Does an ordinary proper-time frequency-shift measurement establish a capability enlargement, or only fixed-family dynamics recorded by a clock?

construction.retention_statement: The assessed object is the ordinary clock record under the same clock family and readout access. Quantum-history certification protocols are excluded from this branch and retained as a separate assessment.

branches.label: ordinary frequency or phase-shift record
branches.normalization_frame: Same clock family, interrogation task, readout access, and control budget; the measured frequency or phase value may change, but the executable task set does not.

assumptions: The transition object is the clock's ordinary frequency or phase record, not a change in available laboratory controls.
The same clock family, interrogation task, readout access, and resource budget are held fixed.
Sorci et al. is used as a theory source and not as evidence of a completed observation.
tests: validate the Transition Diagnosis v0.1 contract
reject capability enlargement when normalized tasks remain equal
falsifiers: the ordinary readout alone performs a predeclared task unavailable to the baseline at the same resources and access
the frequency-shift record cannot be reproduced inside the declared classical or semiclassical proper-time family
the verdict changes when the endpoint labels are exchanged
nonclaims: No proper-time effect is reported here as a new experiment.
No nonclassical proper-time history is certified by a frequency shift alone.
No capability, finality, hierarchy, source-verdict, or canon claim is established.
reopening_conditions: a frozen experiment supplies a matched before-and-after executable task absent from the baseline
a source-backed discriminator rules out the declared classical or semiclassical absorber for the same ordinary record
the resource, access, or control frame changes materially
